picks.name: The Fitness Enthusiast

picks.name: The Affluent Classic
picks.why_plausible: price_sensitivity: low with a $145 typical AOV and a stated preference for quality and longevity over trends fits a $650 shell bought once and kept for a decade; classic_apparel and travel affinities cover ski-trip outerwear. The score ranked her low mainly on publisher reach, not on buying logic — and she also buys gifts for skiing children or partners.
lean_into: craftsmanship and construction quality
buy-once longevity rather than replacing cheap shells
understated, quality-focused tone
picks.ad_angle: Built to outlast the trend cycle: one shell, made properly, worn for seasons rather than replaced.

picks.name: The Wellness Optimizer
picks.why_plausible: price_sensitivity: low with named fitness affinity and outcome-focused messaging preferences fits someone who treats uphill touring as training and wants gear that performs to spec. Weaker than the others because her core categories are supplements and wellness, so the ad must speak to winter training rather than to ski-industry credibility.
lean_into: outcome-focused: stays breathable on the climb, sealed on the descent
specific technical performance rather than vague quality
worth the premium because it performs
avoid: science-backed/clinical proof claims the brief can't support
anything implying casual or sedentary use

campaign.name: Technical ski shells and outerwear for backcountry skiing · post-purchase launch

bid_strategy.rationale: $750 first order × 0.30 = $225.00 target CPA: one-time purchase, so the first order has to pay back the acquisition. The max CPA allows headroom while the campaign learns over 14 days.

frequency_cap.rationale: Offers appear once, right after checkout; repeating them reads as spam.

experiment.graduate_rule: After 14 days, move a test publisher to core if its CPA is at or below target; cut any placement above max CPA.
experiment.notes: Creatives rotate evenly until each has enough conversions to compare.

assumptions: Assumed a typical first order around $750, since prices start at $650 and go up.
Assumed the gear is sold to all adults, as no gender was mentioned.
Assumed one-time purchases rather than a subscription.
Allowable CPA is 30% of first order value (one time); replace with real margin and LTV.
warnings: No publisher in this catalog is a good fit; nothing would run.
